# Driving Growth in Solutions Area: Panasonic HVAC & CC’s Corporate Strategy

- Comprehensive B2B Solution Businesses Across Heating & Ventilation A/C and Cold Chain
- Growing Revenue in Non-Competitive Markets to Support Growth in Competitive Markets
- “Machines In the Field” (MIF): Key for Growth in Solutions Area
- Expanding the Recurring-Revenue Business

Panasonic Group announced its Group Growth Strategy on May 12, 2026, outlining a clear commitment to addressing challenges in areas where it can demonstrate strong competitive power such as using energy more efficiently and alleviating frontline labor shortages. By strengthening businesses that support both AI infrastructure and social operations, the Group plans to accelerate its contributions to society as it looks ahead to 2032.

The Group’s Devices business supports AI infrastructure such as data centers for generative AI, and the company expects this area to be a key driving force behind the Group’s growth. Its Solutions business supports social operations with “always-on, energy- and labor-saving” measures. The Group is transforming its business model and strengthening its service and engineering capabilities to grow the Solutions area into a profit growth core from fiscal year 2030 *1. For this article, Panasonic Newsroom Global spoke with Eiichi Katayama, CEO of Panasonic HVAC & CC Co., Ltd. (HVAC & CC) about the company’s business outlook. HVAC & CC focuses on infrastructure that supports the essentials of daily life—air, water, and food in the Solutions area.

*1. In this article, fiscal years (FY) refer to the years ending March 31 of the stated year.

### Comprehensive B2B Solution Businesses Across Heating & Ventilation A/C and Cold Chain

HVAC & CC was formed in April 2026 by merging two companies that had been within the former Panasonic Corporation: the Heating and Ventilation A/C Company and the Cold Chain Solutions Company. With annual sales of approximately 1.3 trillion yen and a global workforce of about 30,000 employees (as of April 2026), the company operates the businesses related to air, water, and food. HVAC & CC is not a typical air conditioning company. It is a comprehensive solutions provider whose work spans air quality, food distribution, and environmental facilities.

In the Air and Water area, the company offers room air conditioners, commercial air conditioners, indoor air quality (IAQ) *2 products such as ventilation fans and air purifiers, as well as water-related products such as heat pump water heaters and air-to-water heat pumps (A2W) *3. In the Food area, it runs a cold chain business *4 that includes refrigerated and frozen food display cases and commercial kitchen equipment. The company also offers environmental engineering services, such as tunnel ventilation and air purification.

*2. IAQ: Abbreviation for Indoor Air Quality. Refers to products and services related to indoor air quality. *3. A2W: A heat pump system that uses heat from the air to warm water for heating and hot water supply. *4. Cold Chain: A low-temperature logistics system for storing and distributing food, pharmaceuticals, and other items at appropriate temperatures. This includes refrigerated and frozen food display cases, freezers, and related maintenance services.

One distinctive feature of the company is that B2B sales make up roughly 70% of its total revenue—a high proportion even within the Panasonic Group. Katayama points to HVAC & CC’s distribution channels as one of the reasons for this.

Katayama explains, “The room air conditioner business might generally be thought of as B2C. But these units aren’t only bought by individuals at electronics retailers. In many cases, they are installed as part of the infrastructure of homes and buildings by architectural, construction, or facility management companies. We have a vast network of these kinds of supply channels, and because the decisions about selection and installation rest with the business side, we define this as a B2B business.”

 Eiichi Katayama, Representative Director, Board Member, President, Panasonic HVAC & CC Co., Ltd. 

### Growing Revenue in Non-Competitive Markets to Support Growth in Competitive Markets

Katayama acknowledges that combining the heating and ventilation A/C business with the cold chain business is rare, even when looking worldwide, and far from easy. The aim of this reorganization and integration is to strengthen competitiveness in the highly competitive heating and ventilation A/C business by using revenue from profitable, non-competitive areas as a source of capital to support growth.

In the markets HVAC & CC serves, there are areas where the company competes directly with other heating and ventilation A/C manufacturers, and there are non-competitive areas where it can more readily show its unique strengths. The competitive areas include room and commercial air conditioners and A2W. The non-competitive areas include IAQ (such as air purifiers), cold chain, and environmental engineering. “In this newly established company, these two areas account for roughly an even split of revenue, with the non-competitive areas making up about 70% of profits. We will use the non-competitive areas as a foundation for growth while working to expand sales in the competitive areas,” says Katayama.

Katayama cites CO 2 refrigeration units for cold chain—part of the non-competitive areas—as a market poised for medium- to long-term growth. It is already expanding at double-digit rates each year, propelled by shifting demand in response to environmental regulations that are being tightened to address global warming.

Katayama also points to A2W and room air conditioners as key products for driving sales growth in the competitive areas. A2W is currently facing headwinds, but its penetration rate in the European market is still only 5%, and the global penetration rate for room air conditioners is only about half that of refrigerators and washing machines. “Both have strong potential for market growth ahead,” he says.

### “Machines In the Field” (MIF): Key for Growth in Solutions Area

HVAC & CC plays a key role in the Panasonic Group’s growth strategy, which shifts the focus of value creation from hardware to services and expands the Solutions area.

So, what kind of solutions does HVAC & CC provide?

The key term here is Machines In the Field (MIF)—the company’s own equipment and facilities installed and running at customer sites. HVAC & CC places strong emphasis on its MIF as “stock” assets and plans to turn it into a source of recurring revenue. Instead of a “flow” model that earns revenue by selling equipment to new customers, the company is shifting to a recurring-revenue model. Under this approach, the company draws on that “stock” advantage to broaden its range of services and generate steady, long-term revenue. The plan is to make this a core driver of the Panasonic Group’s revenue growth from fiscal year 2030 onward.

HVAC & CC’s hardware is already integrated into the infrastructure of a broad spectrum of corporate clients and public institutions, where it serves as a foundational component supporting critical societal operations.

Beyond that, the company plans to treat room air conditioners that are five or ten years old as valuable assets and to roll out services such as energy-saving proposals around them.

One example of these MIF-based solutions is maintenance and operational support for display cases and freezers in the cold chain area. For equipment already installed in stores, HVAC & CC delivers value by keeping customers’ operations running—through service, maintenance, repair, remote monitoring, and engineering support. The company already offers services such as “ StoreConnect” in the cold chain area.

Another example is “Panasonic HVAC CLOUD,” an AI-powered energy-saving service for commercial air conditioning. Built around air-conditioning equipment, it uses remote management and AI control to deliver energy savings and operational support—turning the equipment’s ongoing operation itself into a continuous point of value for customers.

With its diverse portfolio of MIF, HVAC & CC has a distinctive strength: the ability to manage equipment remotely and offer energy-saving recommendations through software after units are installed—whether those units are network-connected display cases, freezers, heating and ventilation A/C systems, or water heaters. As the scale of MIF expands, there will be more opportunities to contribute to operational and maintenance efficiency, energy savings, and optimization of customers’ cost structures.

HVAC & CC takes three aspects into account when choosing which markets to enter and invest themselves in: “markets with recurring value,” “markets where functionality is emphasized,” and “markets receptive to comprehensive solutions.”

Katayama explains, “We will bring products into the markets featuring our proprietary technologies—such as ‘nanoe’ (hydroxyl radicals contained in water) technology, which helps ensure air quality, and ‘ziaino,’ an air-purification device that uses HOCl (hypochlorous acid) to disinfect and deodorize spaces—into markets where functionality matters most. Beyond that, we’ll draw on our strength in spanning air, water, and food business areas to focus on markets receptive to comprehensive solutions—such as pairing the cold chain with heating and ventilation A/C or pairing IAQ with heating and ventilation A/C.”

Of the 29 trillion yen global market that HVAC & CC addresses, the company is targeting a 4.1 trillion yen segment. Rather than chasing the entire market, the company is concentrating on the segments where it can best demonstrate its value, aiming for steady sales growth in these focus markets by expanding its recurring-revenue Solutions business.

### Expanding the Recurring-Revenue Business

Before HVAC & CC was launched, Katayama led the Sustainable & Climate Tech Group in the former Panasonic Corporation. That group treated fiscal year 2026 as a “year of transition,” and its adjusted operating profit for the year came to just over 33 billion yen. Following that year of transition, HVAC & CC expects its operating profit will nearly double, to 60 billion yen, in fiscal year 2027.

Aiming for further business growth, HVAC & CC will expand its recurring-revenue business—centered on MIF and including service and engineering—and shift toward a revenue model that earns through post hardware sales services and engineering. By maintaining relationships with customers after hardware is sold, the company will strengthen both the stability and the growth potential of its revenue. On using MIF as a driving force for expansion, Katayama notes that this strategy has also been jointly agreed upon with the CEOs of Panasonic Connect Group and Panasonic Electric Works Co., Ltd., other Solutions area companies in the Group. For HVAC & CC, which is positioned within the Solutions area, expanding recurring-revenue businesses will become a key pillar to support the group’s future profit growth.

Under the slogan “HVAC & Cold Chain—Built into Life,” HVAC & CC aims to be the top company in terms of truly understanding its customers. “While different parts of our business have different structures and client bases, our mission is consistent—to stay engaged with customers deeply and broadly and to ensure that their operations never come to a halt,” says Katayama.

The Panasonic Group’s growth strategy lays out its commitment to “Contributing to Society Toward 2032.” The Group is approaching the 100th anniversary of the founder, Konosuke Matsushita, declaring the company’s mission to “achieve an ideal society with affluence both in matter and mind.” The Group is determined to keep supporting “always-on, energy- and labor-saving” social operations by expanding its Solutions area. As one of the driving forces behind this effort, HVAC & CC will contribute to solving social issues and enhancing the Group’s corporate value through continued business growth.

# Panasonic eyes 50% AC sales growth as industry readies 12–15% price hikes 

## Company aims to capitalise on peak summer demand while limiting price hikes for consumers

### By Amit Vijay Mohile

 Updated - March 18, 2026 at 05:55 PM.

 Panasonic currently holds about 7–8% share of India’s room air-conditioner market, trailing Voltas, which commands around 18–20 per cent, and LG Electronics with roughly 17 per cent. | Photo Credit: REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov 

Panasonic India is targeting around 50 per cent growth in air-conditioner sales this year, even as the industry prepares for price increases of 12–15 per cent amid rising input costs and higher logistics expenses linked to the West Asia crisis.

Air-conditioner makers are preparing to raise prices due to higher costs of key raw materials such as copper and aluminium, along with rising logistics costs linked to disruptions in global shipping routes. The expected price hikes also reflect revised energy-efficiency norms introduced by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE).

Video Credit: Businessline

However, Panasonic plans to adopt a more calibrated pricing approach and will not pass on the full cost increase to consumers, said Abhishek Verma, Business Head and Product Chief – AC Group (RAC & CAC) at Panasonic Life Solutions India.

“We believe demand is just about to peak this summer,” Verma said, adding that industry demand could grow around 40 per cent over last year if current trends continue.

Panasonic has recently introduced 57 new air-conditioner models, including units equipped with its Dustbuster technology, which enables self-cleaning of the outdoor unit to improve cooling efficiency.

The company has been consolidating its presence in the premium segment, with about 45 per cent of its current AC sales coming from its smart air-conditioner range. At the same time, Panasonic plans to extend advanced energy-saving technologies and connected features to mid and entry-level models.

“The idea is to democratise energy-efficient and smart features that were earlier limited to premium products and bring them to mid and entry-level segments,” Verma said.

Panasonic currently holds about 7–8 per cent share of India’s room air-conditioner market, trailing Voltas, which commands around 18–20 per cent, and LG Electronics with roughly 17 per cent.

## Market expansion underway

India’s $13–14 billion HVAC market is projected to grow at about 15 per cent annually through the decade, supported by rising incomes, urbanisation and more frequent heatwaves.

Industry estimates suggest that nearly 60 per cent of Indian districts, representing about 76 per cent of the population, are now at very high risk of extreme heat, underscoring the growing need for cooling solutions across the country.

The Indian air-conditioner market is estimated at around 14 million units annually, though penetration remains low at 7–8 per cent of households, making it one of the most underpenetrated cooling markets globally.

The industry, however, witnessed a volatile year in FY26. Unseasonal rains during April and May led to what executives described as a “failed summer”, with several manufacturers reporting volume declines of 25–34 per cent year-on-year in the first quarter as cooling demand weakened.

Demand recovered in the second half of the year, supported by festive sales and pre-buying ahead of energy-efficiency rule changes, putting the industry on track for 10–15 percent revenue growth for the year.

## Localisation and export push

Panasonic has been increasing domestic sourcing for its air conditioners in India. Company executives said domestic value addition has risen from about 25 per cent to nearly 45 per cent, helping reduce import dependence and improve supply-chain resilience.

The company operates its largest manufacturing facility in Jhajjar, Haryana, spread across 76 acres and built with an investment of over ₹1,000 crore, producing air conditioners designed for Indian climatic conditions.

Panasonic also runs the India Innovation Centre in Bengaluru, established in 2018 with an investment of around ₹250 crore, which supports product development and next-generation technologies across its consumer and business solutions portfolio.

Apart from Jhajjar, the company has operations in Sri City, Andhra Pradesh, supporting its broader life solutions business that includes electrical equipment, automation solutions and HVAC products.

Verma said Panasonic is targeting around 1.1 million units in annual AC sales this year, as part of its roadmap to double manufacturing capacity to about 2 million units by FY28 and position India as a regional manufacturing and export hub for markets across Southeast Asia.

The Panasonic India group reported revenue of around ₹11,100 crore and net profit of about ₹1,100 crore in FY25, with consumer goods contributing roughly 30 per cent of total revenue.

# Panasonic reinforces HVAC leadership at ACREX 2026; showcases full-spectrum climate solutions portfolio 

 12-03-2026

- Expanded MirAIe-Enabled VRF Integration and Inverter-Driven iCOOL Cold Chain Range with Multi-Refrigerant Flexibility

New Delhi, 12 th March, 2026: Panasonic Life Solutions India, reinforced its leadership position in the HVAC industry at ACREX India 2026, Asia’s largest HVAC exhibition, unveiling its comprehensive portfolio across Room Air Conditioners (RAC), Commercial Air Conditioning (CAC), VRF systems, and Cold Chain solutions. The showcase reflects Panasonic’s continued focus on delivering intelligent and energy-efficient cooling technologies aligned with India’s evolving infrastructure and sustainability requirements. These components along with the new launches will be exhibited at Booth M-04, Hall 6 at BEC, Mumbai.

At the exhibition, Panasonic is showcasing its integrated climate solutions ecosystem, from smart residential air conditioners powered by the MirAIe connected living platform and AI-enabled VRF systems, to its latest Light Commercial innovations including the new 1-Way Cassette featuring nanoe™ X technology for enhanced indoor air quality. The brand is also highlighting its focus on energy-efficient performance through technologies such as DustBuster, an auto ODU cleaning concept designed to enhance cooling efficiency and extend product life.

Speaking at ACREX 2026, Mr. Hirokazu Kamoda, Managing Director, Panasonic HVAC & CC India, said, "India is one of the fastest-growing HVAC markets in the world, and Panasonic is fully committed to this growth journey. We are expanding our distribution footprint, strengthening our service network, and building deeper partnerships across the country. Our showcase at ACREX reflects our long-term vision to deliver smart, reliable, and future-ready climate solutions across residential, commercial, and cold chain segments.”

Yoshiyuki Kato, Managing Director, Panasonic Electric Works, Panasonic Life Solutions India, said:

“Indoor air quality is increasingly becoming a key determinant of building performance and long-term real estate value. Poorly managed indoor environments can affect occupant comfort, increase complaints, and ultimately impact occupancy and rental potential.

Through technologies such as nanoe™ X and BMS-enabled monitoring and optimisation, Panasonic enables building owners to maintain healthier indoor environments while improving operational efficiency. We believe that investing in better air quality and intelligent building management ultimately supports higher occupancy, stronger tenant satisfaction, and enhanced long-term asset value.”

Commenting on the technology showcase, Mr. Abhishek Verma, Head – Product Marketing & Planning, Panasonic HVAC & CC India, added, "At Panasonic, innovation drives everything we do. From AI-enabled VRF systems and smart connected solutions powered by MirAIe to high-performance light commercial technologies, our portfolio is designed to deliver intelligent control, energy efficiency, and reliability in demanding Indian conditions. ACREX provides us an opportunity to demonstrate how our engineering capabilities are shaping next-generation climate solutions.”

In the cold chain segment, Panasonic is showcasing its iCOOL SE inverter condensing units, engineered for precise temperature management, optimized energy consumption, and enhanced operational efficiency across low- and medium-temperature applications. Designed to deliver performance stability and faster return on investment, the solution addresses the growing need for reliable and scalable cold storage infrastructure across key sectors.

Sharing his views, Mr. Vikas Taneja, Director, Cold Chain, Panasonic HVAC & CC India, said, “India’s cold chain ecosystem is witnessing strong momentum, driven by the rapid expansion of food retail, pharmaceuticals, quick service restaurants, and organized logistics. At Panasonic, we are focused on enabling energy-efficient, high-performance solutions that not only improve product preservation but also reduce operating costs for businesses.”

New Delhi, 12 February 2026: Panasonic Life Solutions India (PLSIND), a leading diversified technology company, today announced the launch of its 2026 lineup of Residential Air Conditioners engineered specifically to tackle the country’s extreme weather conditions. Designed for reliable performance, the new range reflects Panasonic’s focus on delivering durable, energy-efficient, and climate-resilient cooling solutions tailored for Indian homes.

Addressing one of the most persistent challenges impacting AC performance in Indian homes, the new range features Panasonic’s DustBuster Technology, an “auto reverse-flow” fan mechanism designed to automatically expel dust from the outdoor unit, helping maintain consistent cooling, better efficiency and long-term durability. With this technology, Panasonic reinforces its focus on delivering air conditioners that perform reliably even in harsh Indian climatic conditions.

The 2026 portfolio comprises 57 new models across segments and price points, combining performance, energy efficiency, and smart functionality to meet the evolving comfort needs of consumers across the country.

Commenting on the launch, Mr. Hirokazu Kamoda, Managing Director, Panasonic HVAC & CC India, said, “India’s air conditioning market is at a pivotal inflection point, shaped by rapid urbanisation, rising aspirations, and increasingly extreme weather conditions. With our 2026 RAC line-up, we are introducing smarter, more resilient, and energy-efficient air conditioners that go beyond cooling to create healthier and more comfortable living spaces for Indian households. Building on this launch, we aim to scale our air conditioner volumes to approximately 2 million units by FY28, backed by an expanded portfolio, continued investments in technology and manufacturing, and a stronger presence across emerging markets.”

Mr. Abhishek Verma, Head, Product Marketing & Planning, Panasonic HVAC & CC India, said, “With this launch, we are redefining the standards of strong cooling by directly addressing the challenges of heat, dust and tough weather conditions that impact AC performance across India. With 57 new RAC models in CY26, we offer one of the widest portfolios in the industry, spanning over inverter, fixed-speed, smart, hot & cold, and high-capacity solutions. This range further strengthens our commitment to Make in India, focused R&D, and deeper penetration across metro, tier 2, and tier 3 markets.”

The new range includes Panasonic 5-star, 4-star, and 3-star inverter air conditioners, with the 5-star series introducing a premium Amaze Facia design in Dark Grey and Chrome deco, adding a distinctive aesthetic to high-performance cooling. The line-up is available across major retail outlets, leading e-commerce platforms, and the Panasonic brand shop at a starting price of Rs. 32,490/- The launch will be amplified through an ongoing TVC campaign featuring the company’s brand ambassador, India’s ‘Captain Cool’ MS Dhoni, reinforcing the brand’s promise of reliable and resilient cooling for Indian homes. ## Summary

Daikin Industries reported its second-quarter (interim) results for the fiscal year ending March 2027 on November 5, 2026, with revenue up 17.4% year-on-year to ¥2,910.7 billion and operating profit up 9.8% to ¥270.7 billion, marking a record high for the first half. Ordinary profit rose 2.2% to ¥247.1 billion, and interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent increased 7.5% to ¥172.9 billion. Despite cost pressures exceeding initial assumptions—including heightened Middle East tensions, additional US tariffs, soaring raw material prices, and emerging-market currency weakness—the company secured profit growth by expanding sales of high-value-added products, implementing pricing measures, and pursuing total cost reduction, while also capturing the benefits of a weaker yen and US tariff refunds. However, the operating margin fell 0.6 points from 9.9% a year earlier to 9.3%, also falling short of plan.

By segment, the air conditioning and refrigeration business posted revenue of ¥2,699.6 billion, up 17.0% year-on-year, and operating profit of ¥244.3 billion, up 5.2%, achieving revenue and profit growth, but its operating margin declined 1.0 point from 10.1% to 9.1%. By region, Japan (revenue at 118% of the prior year) and Europe (121%) improved profitability through expanded sales of high-value-added products, while the Americas saw its operating margin decline due to tariffs and rising market prices. Asia also saw profitability deteriorate amid higher costs and intensifying competition. The chemical business posted strong sales of high-performance resins for semiconductors and data centers, with revenue up 25.2% to ¥158.7 billion and operating profit up 77.3% to ¥24.2 billion, a substantial profit increase, while its operating margin improved 4.4 points from 10.8% to 15.2%.

The full-year plan was revised upward, with revenue raised from the previous forecast of ¥5,150.0 billion to ¥5,440.0 billion (up 8.5% year-on-year) and operating profit from ¥436.0 billion to ¥455.0 billion (up 9.6%). The company aims to achieve record-high results. The second-half operating margin is expected to improve 0.7 points year-on-year, securing a full-year margin of 8.4%, on par with the prior year. The assumed exchange rates from the third quarter onward are ¥150 per dollar and ¥175 per euro. The annual dividend was raised by ¥10 from the previous forecast to ¥370 per share (interim ¥185, year-end ¥185).

President Naofumi Takenaka identified "re-strengthening earning power" as the top priority, emphasizing five points: transformation into a solution provider, improving profitability of the North American air conditioning business, cost structure reform, efficiency of invested capital, and turnaround of low-profit businesses. Regarding low-profit businesses in particular, he acknowledged that "the speed is insufficient relative to investor expectations" and indicated a policy of reaching early conclusions, including business withdrawal or sale. In North America, data center demand is strong, and revenue from the acquired Alliance Air is also growing. Meanwhile, in China, residential multi-split sales fell to 86% of the prior year amid the real estate downturn, and in Asia, the low-price offensive by Chinese manufacturers is a challenge.

## Operations

### Company-wide results (first half of fiscal 2026)

- Revenue: ¥2,910.7 billion (up 17.4% year-on-year; up 9% excluding FX)
- Operating profit: ¥270.7 billion (up 9.8%; up 7% excluding FX), operating margin 9.3% (down 0.6 points from 9.9% a year earlier)
- Ordinary profit: ¥247.1 billion (up 2.2%)
- Interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent: ¥172.9 billion (up 7.5%)
- FX impact: Revenue +¥200.5 billion, operating profit +¥6.0 billion (dollar-yen 159, euro-yen 184)

### By segment

- Air conditioning and refrigeration business: Revenue ¥2,699.6 billion (up 17.0%), operating profit ¥244.3 billion (up 5.2%), operating margin 9.1% (down 1.0 point from 10.1% a year earlier). Expanded sales of high-value-added products in Japan and Europe contributed, but higher costs and intensifying competition in the Americas and Asia weighed on results.
- Chemical business: Revenue ¥158.7 billion (up 25.2%), operating profit ¥24.2 billion (up 77.3%), operating margin 15.2% (up 4.4 points from 10.8%). High-performance resins for semiconductors and data centers and high-speed communications coating materials performed well.
- Other businesses: Revenue ¥52.3 billion (up 15.8%), operating profit ¥2.2 billion (up 251.3%).

### By region (air conditioning and refrigeration business)

- Japan: Revenue at 118% of the prior year. Residential demand expanded on last-minute demand ahead of energy-saving regulations and subsidies, while commercial demand for heat countermeasures remained firm.
- Americas: Revenue at 117%. DNA (residential) at 114% with a 25% share (up 2 points year-on-year). DAA (applied) at 123%, with data center demand growing significantly.
- China: Revenue at 105%. Residential multi-split fell to 86%, but commercial and applied products compensated, keeping the operating margin at a high level.
- Europe: Revenue at 121%. Significant revenue growth on heatwave demand and a recovery in heat pump heating.
- Asia and Oceania: Asia at 123% (India at 139%), Oceania at 126%. However, profitability declined due to higher costs and currency weakness.

### Financial position and cash flow

- Total assets: ¥5,841.5 billion (up ¥32.2 billion from the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Equity ratio: 51.0% (down from 55.9% at the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Interest-bearing debt ratio: 22.8% (up from 18.8% at the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Operating cash flow: ¥341.0 billion inflow (up ¥97.6 billion year-on-year)
- Share buyback: ¥350.0 billion executed (May 2026)

### Factors behind operating profit change (year-on-year)

- FX +¥6.0 billion, raw materials -¥77.0 billion (including direct US tariff impact of -¥10.3 billion and refunds of +¥12.6 billion), fixed costs and others -¥35.0 billion, sales expansion +¥49.2 billion, pricing measures +¥46.0 billion, cost reduction +¥35.0 billion.

## Outlook

### Full-year earnings forecast (fiscal year ending March 2027, revised)

- Revenue: ¥5,440.0 billion (up 8.5% year-on-year; revised up 5.6% from the previous forecast of ¥5,150.0 billion)
- Operating profit: ¥455.0 billion (up 9.6%; revised up 4.4% from the previous forecast of ¥436.0 billion), operating margin 8.4% (up 0.1 point from 8.3% a year earlier)
- Ordinary profit: ¥417.0 billion (up 2.2%)
- Net profit attributable to owners of the parent: ¥280.0 billion (up 1.7%)
- Net profit per share: ¥1,006.45
- Assumed exchange rates: From the third quarter onward, ¥150 per dollar and ¥175 per euro

### Full-year plan by segment

- Air conditioning and refrigeration business: Revenue ¥5,003.0 billion (up 8% year-on-year), operating profit ¥404.0 billion (up 7%), operating margin 8.1%. In North America, the company will expand sales and share of residential unitary products, strengthen Fit's sales capabilities, and expand data center solutions.
- Chemical business: Revenue ¥320.0 billion (up 14%), operating profit ¥45.0 billion (up 36%), operating margin 14.1%. Expand sales for semiconductors and data centers.

### Key initiatives for the second half

- Reap the benefits of pricing measures and cost reductions implemented in the first half during the second half, improving the operating margin by 0.7 points year-on-year.
- Improve the operating margin of the North American air conditioning business by 1 point for the full year (from 11% in the first half to the full-year target). Absorb cost increases through expanding Fit dealers and increasing sales per store, pricing measures, and total cost reduction.
- For data centers, three-quarters of the order backlog is already under construction, and the business impact in fiscal 2027 is expected to be limited. For the order backlog from fiscal 2028 onward, the company will begin evaluating each project individually.
- For low-profit businesses (a dozen or so businesses including the filter business and the European low-temperature business), the company will reach early conclusions, including withdrawal or sale.
- Share buybacks will not be capped at ¥700.0 billion; the company will act flexibly, prioritizing growth investments while also considering asset sales and leverage.
- The annual dividend is ¥370 per share (interim ¥185, year-end ¥185), raised by ¥10 from the previous forecast.

## Q&A Highlights

Q: What is the top-line outlook and competitive environment for Japan, Europe, and Asia?
A: In Japan, demand swelled on last-minute demand ahead of energy-saving regulations and the expansion of Tokyo Metropolitan Government subsidies, and we secured supply and fully captured the benefits. Assuming a backlash next year, we are already strengthening commercial products and addressing routes and regions where room air conditioner share is low. In Europe, we captured heatwave demand through our local production system, contributing to profit mainly in the mid-to-high-end segment. Chinese manufacturers are mounting a low-price offensive, but we differentiate ourselves in the mid-to-high-end segment. In Asia, the top line grew on recovering demand in India, but profitability declined due to Chinese manufacturers' low-price offensive, higher costs, and currency weakness. Toward next fiscal year, we will advance a three-tier strategy (premium, mid-range, and mass-market) and strengthen commercial and applied products.

Q: What is the balance between price pass-through and share for US DNA?
A: The housing market is tough due to high mortgage rates, but our policy of prioritizing profitability will not waver. We will increase the mix of high-value-added products such as Fit and strengthen light commercial and parts/solutions. Leveraging our strongest-in-North-America product lineup including R32-compatible products and VRV, we will also advance AI-driven labor savings and optimization of our branch network to ensure we raise the margin. We will maintain share while focusing on price and mix.

Q: What is driving the sales expansion effect as a profit contributor?
A: Expanded sales of high-value-added products and solutions in Europe, Asia, and Japan contributed. In North America, the consumption environment is weak and demand is shifting to cheaper products, limiting mix improvement. In the second half, factory utilization will rise on higher volumes, while production will decrease due to inventory efficiency efforts.

Q: What are the risks to data center demand and the impact of environmental policy?
A: There may be policy changes after the midterm elections, but the impact this fiscal year is limited with only five months remaining. In fiscal 2027 as well, three-quarters of the order backlog is under construction, so the impact is limited. For fiscal 2028, we will begin evaluating each project individually. The Mexico plant will have a flexible line configuration resilient to demand fluctuations, and the new plant will be established on a lease basis with investment decisions made in stages. On the environmental front, we recognize that rising electricity prices and power shortages will be tailwinds for energy-saving, high-efficiency products.

Q: How did you offset the first-half cost increases? What are the upside factors for the full-year plan?
A: In the first half, we implemented additional cost improvements in response to cost increases exceeding assumptions. We also reduced fixed costs company-wide compared with the original plan. For the full year, the structure is to cover what pricing measures cannot fully offset through cost reduction and fixed-cost efficiency. The long-term fixed-cost reduction themes of FUSION30 will bear fruit in the latter half, but the current positive results are largely due to the accumulated efforts of each department.

Q: What is the background behind the ¥90.0 billion sales expansion effect?
A: We are not pursuing volume expansion that ignores profitability, but in the past there were unprofitable products. Under FUSION30, we do not assume significant demand growth and are promoting efforts to increase the weight of high-value-added products in all regions. Since price revisions involve large cost increases, we respond by moving up new product launches, among other measures. To counter Chinese manufacturers' entry into the volume zone, we will strengthen product and sales capabilities and cost competitiveness.

Q: What is the breakdown and profitability of the 28% solution business ratio?
A: The ratio is to global air conditioning business revenue. The composition ratio of residential to commercial is 1:3 to 1:3.5. Commercial solutions grew more than 10% in the first half, but residential declined year-on-year due to lower residential multi-split sales in China. The profit margin of commercial solutions is not significantly different from that of equipment, but maintenance and parts have high gross margins, and we will improve profitability through scale expansion. Quantitative targets are not disclosed at this time.

Q: What are India's profit margin and competitive environment?
A: India's profit margin was about 8% last fiscal year, lower than other regions, and we aim to raise it to 10% or more during the FUSION30 period. Currently, rupee weakness is increasing procurement costs and slightly worsening profitability, but this is not a structural factor. We are promoting dealer development not only at the first tier but also at the second tier, leveraging the superiority of our product lineup. The challenge is the high proportion of residential products, so we will increase the commercial ratio. Our biggest rival is local manufacturers, and Chinese manufacturers are entering through OEM. We will increase the mix of system products and commercial products for affluent customers.

Q: What are the future risks of raw material costs?
A: Copper, initially assumed at $12,000 per ton, has risen to around $13,500, and we have incorporated a negative factor of over ¥10.0 billion. Parts, mainly resins, are also affected by inflation more than copper, and we expect cost increases of over ¥20.0 billion. For this fiscal year, about 70% of both copper and aluminum is hedged, but hedging for next fiscal year is not progressing, and we will prepare the budget assuming raw material prices continue to rise next fiscal year. We will accelerate substitution from copper to other materials.

Q: What is the certainty of achieving the second-half profit increase and what is the story on the ground?
A: Fit is completely different from conventional US products, so it took time, but we continue to provide detailed support globally, including installation support for the first 10 units, standing fully behind dealers. We are moving up the development and launch of differentiated products and following up monthly with individual action plans that achieve price, volume, and mix simultaneously. The field understands our system of taking additional measures in response to environmental changes.

Q: What is your thinking on next fiscal year's operating margin?
A: Copper prices are not sufficiently hedged for next fiscal year, so we are prepared for some cost increases. Fit sales expansion has been growing since the second quarter and we have high expectations for next year. Commercial solutions are also expected to improve profit as maintenance and other services grow with expansion. For next fiscal year, we are working with each business line to concretize profit growth without expecting significant revenue growth. In DNA, low-SEER products are increasing, so we will reduce costs on the growing products while firmly selling high-value-added products. For rooftop products, which are easy to install, we will launch new inverter-equipped products. We will reduce fixed costs through DX-driven labor savings and branch network optimization, positioning next fiscal year as the year to fully reap the results.

Q: Is the decline in the chemical business's second-half margin due to seasonality?
A: Production capacity is becoming quite tight, and we are considering whether we can expand sales while maintaining high efficiency. We are telling the business unit that it can do a little better in the second half.

Q: What is the competitive environment for data centers and how are acquired technologies being utilized?
A: Data center sales grew about 1.5 times from the prior year, mainly chillers. The acquired Alliance Air (custom AHUs) also grew about 40%, and the server rack cooling company grew nearly threefold. We are advancing communication with hyperscalers and strengthening packaged, modular, and containerized offerings to meet short construction and delivery needs. Competition is intense with power equipment manufacturers also entering, but we will compete through systematization leveraging our strengths.

AC Price Guide India 2026: 1, 1.5 & 2 Ton

# AC Price Guide India: What Should a 1, 1.5 and 2 Ton AC Cost?

 Aquib Nawab

October 28, 2026

There is no single “correct” AC price in India because tonnage is only one part of the equation. Star rating, inverter technology, cooling capacity, smart controls, construction, warranty and even the AC series can move the price considerably. As a practical reference, current Haier India models span from ₹35,990 for an approximately 1-ton AC to around ₹50,990 for selected 1.5-ton and approximately 2-ton models.

That difference matters. Comparing air conditioners only by tonnage can make a cheaper machine look like the obvious buy when, in reality, the two products may offer very different efficiency ratings, controls and cooling capabilities.

Here is a more useful way to read AC prices before spending your money.

## How Much Does an AC Cost in India in 2026?

For buyers comparing Haier air conditioners, the current examples below offer a useful snapshot of how prices change across capacities and configurations.

| AC category | Haier model example | Star rating | Listed price* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Ton | Kinouchi Ultra AI Smart AC, HSA14KU-CAI4NB-I | 4 Star | ₹35,990 |
| 1.5 Ton | Kinouchi Heavy Duty AI Smart AC, HSA19KHD-GAI3NB-I | 3 Star | ₹44,990 |
| 1.5 Ton | Galaxy Slate Gravity Heavy Duty AI Smart AC, HSA19GHD-DAI5NB-I | 5 Star | ₹50,990 |
| 2 Ton | Kinouchi Heavy Duty AI Smart AC, HSA24KHD-RAI3NB-I | 3 Star | ₹50,990 |

*Prices shown are the prices listed on the Haier India product pages on 29 September 2026 and may change with offers, availability or promotional periods.

Already, something interesting appears: tonnage alone does not determine the price. A premium 1.5-ton 5-Star model can cost the same as a higher-capacity 2-ton 3-Star model because specification, efficiency and product positioning also affect what you pay.

## What Is the Cost of a 1 Ton AC?

Credits: Haier India

A current Haier example puts an approximately 1-ton smart inverter AC at ₹35,990. The Kinouchi Ultra HSA14KU-CAI4NB-I has a 0.97-ton rated capacity, 4-Star rating and ISEER of 5.05.

For many buyers, this capacity becomes relevant when cooling a relatively compact room, although room area should never be the only deciding factor. Sun exposure, ceiling height, number of occupants, windows and local climate all change the actual cooling load.

The more useful question is not simply, “Can I get a 1-ton AC cheaply?” It is:

What am I getting for that price?

In this Haier model, the feature package includes AI-ATMOX-based climate management, Hexa Inverter technology, app and voice controls, 7-in-1 convertible cooling and a claimed 20-metre air flow.

So, for someone trying to keep the purchase comfortably below ₹50,000, an approximately 1-ton model can leave reasonable headroom without automatically reducing the decision to entry-level cooling.

## How Much Is a 1.5 Ton AC Price?

This is where the answer becomes less tidy and more useful.

Two current Haier examples show why searching for one universal 1.5 ton AC price can be misleading.

The Kinouchi Heavy Duty AI Smart AC HSA19KHD-GAI3NB-I is listed at ₹44,990. It carries a 3-Star rating, 1.48-ton capacity and ISEER of 4.35.

Move to the Galaxy Slate Gravity Series HSA19GHD-DAI5NB-I and the listed price rises to ₹50,990. Its specification changes too: approximately 1.46-ton capacity, 5-Star rating and ISEER 5.65, along with a premium fabric-finish design.

That roughly ₹6,000 difference is therefore not simply a markup for “another 1.5-ton AC”. You are looking at different efficiency levels and product configurations.

### Which 1.5-ton option makes more sense?

Think in terms of usage rather than sticker price alone.

- Moderate usage: A lower-priced configuration can make sense when the AC will not run for extremely long periods every day.
- Heavy summer usage: A higher-efficiency model deserves closer attention because operating cost becomes more relevant over years of ownership.
- Design-conscious rooms: Finish and appearance may matter when the indoor unit is going into a carefully designed living room or bedroom.
- Smart-home users: App control, voice compatibility and energy monitoring can carry real everyday value if you actually use them.

The wrong move is paying extra for features that will sit untouched. The other wrong move? Saving a few thousand upfront while ignoring the efficiency or capability you genuinely need.

## Which AC Is Best for a Home Under ₹50,000?

There is no universally “best” model for every home under ₹50,000. The stronger shortlist depends on room cooling requirement and expected usage.

Within the Haier examples covered here, two straightforward options sit below that mark:

### Around ₹35,990: Kinouchi Ultra approximately 1 Ton

A sensible candidate where lower capacity is appropriate and the buyer still wants smart functionality, inverter operation and a 4-Star configuration.

### Around ₹44,990: Kinouchi Heavy Duty approximately 1.5 Ton

This moves into a higher cooling-capacity bracket while remaining below ₹50,000. The model includes features such as 7-in-1 convertible operation, Supersonic Cooling, AI-based controls and smart app functionality. 

A ₹50,000 budget, in other words, can cover considerably more than simply “basic AC plus remote”. But room requirements must come first. Buying an undersized AC simply to stay inside a budget can be a false saving if the unit has to work harder to maintain comfort.

## What Should a 2 Ton AC Cost?

Haier’s 2-ton Kinouchi Heavy Duty AI Smart AC, HSA24KHD-RAI3NB-I, is listed at ₹50,990 in the product information.

Its technical specification lists 1.79-ton capacity, 6.3 kW cooling capacity, 3-Star rating and ISEER 4.35.

That last detail is worth noticing. Consumer categories such as “2 ton” are often easier to shop by, but the detailed specification tells you the rated capacity of the actual product.

Higher-capacity machines tend to be considered for larger spaces or rooms with more substantial cooling loads. Still, automatically buying the largest AC you can afford is not a clever shortcut. Oversizing and undersizing both deserve to be avoided; proper capacity selection matters.

## Why Are Some ACs So Expensive?

Credits: Haier India

Because you are not really buying “cold air by the ton”.

Several components can push the price upwards.

### Energy-efficiency specification

Higher-efficiency models can carry different hardware and engineering requirements. Buyers should look beyond the star graphic and compare the stated ISEER of the exact model.

### Inverter system

Inverter ACs continuously vary compressor operation rather than relying only on simple on/off cycles. Haier’s featured models use Hexa Inverter technology.

### Smart features

Features such as app operation, voice control, usage monitoring and automatic climate adjustment add another layer of functionality beyond basic temperature selection.

### Extreme-weather performance

Indian summers can be severe. The Haier models covered here state cooling performance at ambient temperatures up to 60°C, alongside protective technologies such as Hyper PCB and anti-corrosion treatment.

### Air distribution

Cooling a room is not simply about making the evaporator cold. How effectively cooled air travels through the room matters too. The referenced Kinouchi and Gravity models feature a claimed air flow of up to 20 metres.

And then there is construction: copper heat exchangers, protective coatings, filters, outdoor-unit design and the compressor itself. Much of what you are paying for is hidden behind the casing.

## How Much Is 1 Ton in kW?

One ton of refrigeration is approximately 3.517 kW of cooling capacity. It does not mean that a 1-ton AC consumes 3.517 kW of electricity continuously.

This distinction trips up plenty of buyers.

“Ton” describes cooling capacity. Electrical power consumption is a different figure and depends on the AC’s design, operating load, efficiency and conditions.

For example, Haier’s approximately 1-ton Kinouchi Ultra model HSA14KU-CAI4NB-I is specified with 3,400 W of 100% cooling capacity, which sits close to the cooling-capacity range expected from its 0.97-ton rating. 

So do not convert tonnage directly into your electricity bill. That calculation needs more information.

## How Much Does AC Installation Cost in India?

Credits: Haier India

There is no responsible single figure that applies to every installation.

Installation cost can change depending on the model, offer, site conditions and whether extra work or material is needed. Additional copper piping, drain arrangements, electrical work, wall conditions or outdoor-unit placement can all affect the final requirement.

For example, the current Galaxy Slate Gravity HSA19GHD-DAI5NB-I model page specifically lists free installation as part of its offer.

That does not mean every AC, installation scenario or future offer carries the same terms.

Before placing an order, check the exact product page and applicable installation conditions rather than budgeting from an old number seen online.

## Why Is AC Gas Costly?

What people casually call “AC gas” is refrigerant. The refrigerant itself is only one part of a service bill.

If refrigerant has been lost, a competent service process may need to identify why. Refrigerant normally circulates within a sealed system, so repeatedly topping it up without understanding the underlying issue is not a meaningful long-term fix.

The Haier models referenced in this guide use R32 refrigerant. 

Service cost can therefore involve refrigerant quantity, diagnosis, labour and repair requirements rather than the refrigerant alone.

## Price Is the Starting Point. Ownership Is the Real Comparison.

A ₹36,000 AC and a ₹51,000 AC are not automatically cheap and expensive versions of the same thing.

Look at the complete package:

- Correct cooling capacity for your room
- Star rating and ISEER
- Expected daily usage
- Inverter technology
- Airflow and cooling performance
- Smart controls you will genuinely use
- Construction and heat-exchanger specification
- Warranty terms
- Installation conditions
- Current offers

Haier’s current range illustrates how that choice can scale. Buyers can start with the approximately 1-ton, 4-Star Kinouchi Ultra at ₹35,990, move into the 1.5-ton Kinouchi Heavy Duty at ₹44,990, consider the 5-Star Galaxy Slate Gravity at ₹50,990, or step up in capacity with the approximately 2-ton Kinouchi Heavy Duty at ₹50,990.

Rather than chasing the lowest price on the screen, match the AC to the room first and then compare what you receive for the money. That is usually where a more sensible purchase begins.

### What is the price of a 1-ton AC in India?

A current Haier example, the approximately 1-ton Kinouchi Ultra AI Smart AC, is listed at ₹35,990. Its rated capacity is 0.97 ton, with a 4-Star rating and 5.05 ISEER.

### What is the price of a 1.5-ton AC in India?

Current Haier examples show that 1.5-ton AC prices can vary significantly by specification. A 3-Star Kinouchi Heavy Duty model is listed at ₹44,990, while a 5-Star Galaxy Slate Gravity model is listed at ₹50,990.

### How much does a 2-ton AC cost in India?

A current Haier approximately 2-ton Kinouchi Heavy Duty AI Smart AC is listed at ₹50,990. Its detailed specification gives a rated capacity of 1.79 ton, 6.3 kW cooling capacity, 3-Star rating and 4.35 ISEER.

### Is a 1-ton AC enough for a room?

It depends on the room’s cooling load rather than floor area alone. Factors such as room size, sunlight exposure, ceiling height, windows, insulation, occupancy and local climate should be considered before choosing capacity.

### Which is better: a 3-Star or 5-Star AC?

Synopsis

Haier India has introduced its new Gravity AI Series air conditioners. These premium units feature AI-driven climate personalisation and predictive cooling. The series also includes India's first fully automatic outdoor unit cleaning system. Haier is expanding its manufacturing and aims for a significant share of the AC market by 2030.

ET Online

Haier launches Gravity AI AC series with India’s first auto-clean outdoor unit

Haier Appliances India on Friday unveiled its Gravity AI Series air conditioners, said to be the company’s most premium and AI-integrated line yet. Powered by the new AI-AtmoX platform, the series introduces features such as AI-driven climate personalisation, predictive cooling and India’s first fully automatic outdoor-unit cleaning system.According to Haier, the Gravity AI Series uses AI-AtmoX across three layers: energy savings, comfort and service. These help deliver real-time power optimisation, adaptive cooling based on user behaviour, and automated self-cleaning for both indoor and outdoor units. “Our Gravity AI Series represents the next frontier in AI-driven appliances,” said NS Satish, President, Haier Appliances India. He added that 90% of Haier’s products are now locally made as part of its “Made in India, Made for India” strategy, which includes strengthening component localisation for a more agile supply chain.

Satish said Haier has shifted almost entirely to digital in its marketing strategy. “We haven’t released even a single print ad in 2025,” he told ET Online. The brand is using AI tools to speed up creative turnaround, personalise campaigns and optimise spending across digital, connected TV and sports-entertainment properties, backed by in-market pushes through e-commerce and Haier’s own direct-to-consumer channels.He added that air conditioners are the appliance category that stands to benefit the most from AI because they can sense, clean and optimise cooling dynamically. At the same time, Haier is pushing AI across its broader portfolio from televisions and washing machines to refrigerators, as it works to build an interconnected device ecosystem.

### Live Events

Satish said this multi-category approach is also helping Haier build its own interconnected device ecosystem, joining the likes of Samsung and Xiaomi in trying to create cross-device control inside Indian homes. “Today our devices can talk to each other,” he said. “If you have a television, you can control your air conditioner. If you have a washing machine, you can control it through the TV. The refrigerator can be controlled through the TV as well.”

Haier believes this interoperability will help deepen customer engagement and extend the lifetime value of its users.

Satish also noted that AI’s value goes beyond hardware performance, calling it a brand mover. “AI pushes the brand up,” he said, adding that it helps attract consumers who prioritise comfort and convenience over traditional specs. Haier sees AI as a tool for premiumisation and stronger consumer stickiness, rather than something that can be tied to a specific growth percentage.The Gravity AI Series starts at Rs 49,990 and will be available across online and offline retailers in four colour variants: Morning Mist, Moon Stone Grey, Midnight Dream and White.

ET Online

ET Online was also at Haier's air conditioner factory.

Haier is simultaneously scaling up its manufacturing footprint. With Phase 2 of its AC plant and a new injection-moulding facility coming online at Greater Noida in early 2026, the company’s annual AC capacity will rise from 1.5 million units to 4 million by 2027.The brand, which currently holds an 8% share of India’s AC market, is targeting 17% by 2030.

# Samsung, LG Launch AI Air Conditioner Battle as Another Scorching Summer Looms

Published 2026.02.06. 06:00:05

By Kim Yoon-soo

Samsung and LG launch 'AI air conditioner' battle early in the year as sweltering heat predicted again this summer

Samsung and LG launch 'AI air conditioner' battle early in the year as sweltering heat predicted again this summer

Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and LG Electronics (066570.KS), Korea's two largest home appliance makers, are racing to capture air conditioner demand from the start of the year as another sweltering summer is forecast following last year's heat waves.

With air conditioners becoming an always-on appliance like smartphones amid increasingly severe summers, both companies are focusing their marketing on artificial intelligence features that enable easy operation, automatic airflow adjustment, and even cleaning assistance.

Samsung Electronics unveiled its new stand-type air conditioner "Bespoke AI WindFree Combo Gallery Pro" and wall-mounted "Bespoke AI WindFree Combo Pro Wall-Mount" at the Seoul R&D Campus in Seocho-gu on Sunday. The new products feature AI-powered user motion detection, usage pattern learning, and more diverse airflow control options.

The AI suggests whether to turn on the unit when users return home after going out. It also switches to long-range airflow when users are far away. Through pattern learning, it recommends indirect wind or WindFree mode instead of direct airflow for users who stay in one place for extended periods, like students studying for exams. Conversely, it provides strong airflow for users who are sensitive to heat and prioritize rapid cooling.

Samsung supports six airflow modes: direct, indirect, and WindFree, as well as "Circulation" which rotates to cool wide spaces evenly, "Long-Range" which sends cool air up to 8.5 meters, and "Max" which cools 19% faster than previous models. The company also introduced a motion radar sensor for the first time that can detect user movement every second.

Enhanced AI voice assistant "Bixby" now enables conversational commands. The "Wearable Good Sleep" feature, which adjusts airflow during sleep in conjunction with Galaxy Watch, is also supported. Prices range from 4.02 million to 7.3 million won for stand-type models.

"The annual number of heat wave days is approaching 30," said Shin Moon-sun, Vice President of Samsung Electronics' Home Appliance Division. "Air conditioners have become appliances that you keep running continuously rather than turning on and off."

LG Electronics' new "LG Whisen Objet Collection Tower I" and "LG Whisen Objet Collection View I Pro," launched last month, feature "AI Cold Free" technology for the first time in the series. This function allows AI to simultaneously control cooling and dehumidification. Conventional air conditioners have the drawback of humidity rising during prolonged cooling, and temperature rising again when dehumidifying to address this. AI Cold Free operates the air conditioner while balancing temperature and humidity.

LG Electronics also introduced various AI features including "AI Wind" which adjusts airflow by detecting user location and patterns via radar sensor, "AI Sleep" which adjusts according to sleep patterns, "AI Voice Recognition" based on GPT models to understand user intent, and "Away Energy Saving" which detects when users leave and reduces energy consumption by 77%. "AI Heat Exchanger Cleaning," which analyzes data measured by humidity and temperature sensors to assess heat exchanger contamination and automatically cleans it, is also supported. Prices range from 5.45 million to 5.97 million won for the Tower I.

According to the Korea Meteorological Administration's "2026 Annual Climate Outlook," there is a 70% probability that this year's average temperature will be higher than normal (12.3-12.7 degrees Celsius). With a 0% probability of temperatures being below normal, hot weather is virtually guaranteed.

## One system. Four seasons.

These are air-to-air heat pumps, not just summer air conditioners. They cool when it’s hot, give you fast and highly efficient heating when it’s cold, and dehumidify whenever excess moisture becomes a problem.

### A smarter way to heat the rooms you actually use

Your central heating is designed to heat the whole house. That’s not always what you need.

Instead, keep your home at a comfortable background temperature — say 18°C — then use your LG system to rapidly bring the rooms you’re actually using up to 21°C.

Because a heat pump moves heat rather than generating it directly, it can deliver several units of heat for every unit of electricity consumed. Depending on energy prices, outside temperature and your existing heating system, that can make heating an occupied room with your LG cheaper than turning up the gas boiler to heat the whole house.

It’s particularly effective alongside underfloor heating. UFH is wonderfully comfortable and efficient at holding a steady temperature, but its high thermal mass means it can take many hours to respond. Let the underfloor maintain a solid background temperature, and use your LG for the rapid few degrees of extra warmth when and where you want it.

### And when it’s wet outside?

Switch to dehumidification.

Dry washing indoors and your clothes can release litres of water into the air — moisture that otherwise ends up as condensation on windows, damp surfaces and eventually mould.

Your LG can pull that excess moisture out of the room while you dry your washing, helping keep the house comfortable without opening the windows and throwing away all that heat.

Cooling in summer. Heating in winter. Humidity control in between. That’s why we think of these as year-round climate systems — not just air conditioning.

Daikin Industries: one of the most important peers in HVAC and climate systems, particularly in commercial air and high-specification installations. Sony Group: a key premium peer in televisions and home entertainment, especially at the high end of the display market. Harman International: a relevant competitor in automotive infotainment, cockpit electronics, and connected-car systems. # Midea Targets Summer Power Bills With New Smart Air Conditioner Range

 Emma Wheaton | 29 Oct 2026 

 

Midea has launched the Edith Series, its new range of air conditioners that combine AI-powered energy management, rapid cooling and smart home controls, in the lead up to a hot Australian summer. 

The Edith Series has six reverse-cycle split-system models with the company claiming its Heat/Cool Flash technology can lower room temperatures by 6°C in just 10 minutes. 

Another feature, its AI ECOMASTER system, uses algorithms trained on billions of data points to maintain more consistent temperatures and reduce wasted energy.

Sensitive to the cost of living and higher summer energy bills, Midea is also offering energy monitoring through its SmartHome app, which allows users to track electricity consumption and manage their air conditioning remotely.

Midea’s Edith Series includes Wi-Fi connectivity and voice control compatibility with Google Home and Amazon Alexa. A temperature sensor built into the remote control works with the Follow Me feature to help regulate room conditions based on the temperature around the user rather than relying solely on the indoor unit’s sensor.

The handy Wind Avoid Me function redirects air away from occupants, while automatic vertical and horizontal swing distributes cooled or heated air throughout the room.

The range also features air-cleaning capabilities. Its I-Clean Pro system uses a six-step evaporator cleaning process, followed by high-temperature steam treatment at 56°C for more than 30 minutes. According to Midea, the process reduces bacteria trapped on the coils by 99.9%.

The Edith range is built on Midea’s Prime Guard platform, which includes a graphene coating, refrigerant leakage detection and automatic restart functionality. The company says the system is designed to operate in outdoor temperatures of up to 50°C, a consideration for Australian conditions during extreme heat.

Outdoor Silent mode is another feature, with Midea claiming it reduces outdoor unit noise by between three and seven decibels.

The new range covers cooling capacities from 2.1kW to 8.0kW, with heating capacities ranging from 2.5kW to 8.7kW.

Pricing starts at $899 for the 2.1kW cooling model, rising to $999 for the 2.5kW unit, $1,299 for the 3.5kW model, $1,699 for the 5.2kW system and $1,899 for the 7.0kW version. The flagship 8.0kW cooling model is priced at $2,399.

The new Midea Edith Series is available now.

# Midea highlights compact kitchen appliances for winter 

 Fri, 8th May 2026 

 MARK TARRE News Chief 

Midea has highlighted four kitchen appliances for winter cooking and cleaning in Australia, centred on compact household products for everyday meal preparation.

The line-up includes a 6L Multi Pressure Cooker, a 5L Induction Rice Cooker, a 45L Smart Inverter Microwave and a benchtop mini dishwasher, with retail prices ranging from AUD $149 to AUD $599.

The lowest-priced item is the 6L Multi Pressure Cooker at AUD $149. It has 12 preset cooking functions for dishes such as meat, broth, beans and oatmeal.

It also includes a 24-hour delay timer, a non-stick inner pot and safety features including a lid lock, pressure-limiting valve and overheat protection. The product is sold through Amazon.

Kitchen range

The 5L Induction Rice Cooker is priced at AUD $199 and available through Bing Lee, Electrical Discounters and Amazon. Designed for more than rice preparation, it also includes settings for porridge and steamed dishes.

According to the product details, the rice cooker has a 10-cup capacity and 10 preset menus. It also uses what Midea calls Omni-Dimensional IH Technology, a Turbo Convection Valve and a 2.0mm multi-layer inner pot.

The 45L Smart Inverter Microwave has a recommended retail price of AUD $239 and is positioned for households seeking faster cooking and reheating across a broad range of common meals.

Its listed features include Smart Inverter Technology, a humidity sensor, 10 power levels and preset options for foods including popcorn, pasta, rice, vegetables, potatoes and pizza. It is stocked by Bing Lee and Electrical Discounters.

Compact cleaning

The highest-priced product is the Midea Benchtop Mini Dishwasher at AUD $599, aimed at smaller homes, apartments, dormitory settings and other spaces where a compact dishwashing unit may be useful.

The dishwasher holds three place settings and includes a built-in 5L water tank, meaning it does not require plumbing. Midea also lists touchscreen controls, a 58-minute quick wash, a 77-minute self-clean cycle, a baby-care mode, fan drying and automatic door opening at the end of cycles.

Seasonal push

The product selection reflects a seasonal retail push around colder weather and more time spent cooking at home. The emphasis is on smaller appliances for meal preparation, reheating and clean-up rather than major whitegoods.

Midea presented the range as a mix of multi-function cooking devices and space-saving kitchen equipment, targeting households looking for practical appliances at relatively modest price points.

No sales figures or broader Australian market plans were disclosed alongside the product list. Instead, the announcement focused on feature sets, household use cases and retailer availability across online and in-store channels.

Midea said its products are designed to save time, be energy efficient and not break the bank.

# Designed for Living: How We Positioned Midea as a Premium Home Tech Brand

 3 Mar 

Written by Allison Thuang

 

 distillery partnered with Midea to create a comprehensive marketing toolkit, boosting brand perception for home appliances across the APAC region. 

Despite $56 billion USD in 2024 annual revenue, global sponsorships, and a portfolio of global consumer tech brands suite, Midea’s target audience still preferred splurging on Samsung and LG when outfitting their kitchens. 

The challenge was not product capability: it was brand perception.

And, with a new home appliance range poised for launch across APAC, Midea needed to rewrite that story fast.

### The Brief

Midea came to us with a desire to shift positioning for Suite 1.0 - a comprehensive, AI-powered home appliance ecosystem designed for couples and young families. 

The product was premium yet accessible, tech-focused and genuinely innovative. But… the market didn't know it yet. 

The JBTD? Create a campaign toolkit powerful enough to work across multiple markets, flexible enough for local activation, and compelling enough to launch Midea onto the shortlist for first home owners, families and appliance upgraders across APAC. 

The stakes were high. This wasn't just a campaign: it was a factory reset button for an entire region.

### Our Approach

We developed a comprehensive marketing and sales toolkit designed to empower local markets to bring Suite 1.0 to life in ways that felt both global and intimate. 

Our strategy was powered by a fundamental insight: home appliances aren't about the products themselves. They're about the life they enable - the big moments, the mundane moments and everything in between - to create within four walls.

 

So, with this in mind, we built the campaign around three integrated pillars:

- Aspiration: Positioning Suite 1.0 as the undisputable first (or second) choice for modern couples and families who didn’t want to compromise on tech or design features
- Accessibility: Proving that premium tech didn’t require a premium price, and that Suite 1.0 could be both sophisticated and attainable.
- Connection: Emphasizing that AI could understand and adapt to how folks actually lived, not how product managers and engineers imagined they would.

Our creative strategy centered on the concept of "AI That Cares”, allowing our teams to move beyond technical specs to showcase Midea's emotional value. 

To strengthen this, we developed a visual language that felt premium and aspirational while remaining warm and human. The "SmartMaster" product line became the hero, but always in the context of artfully composed homes where real people lived their real lives.

### The Experience

The toolkit we delivered was designed to work across the full customer journey from awareness to consideration to conversion.

Films formed the creative backbone—a series of 11 films (ranging from 15 seconds to the main hero film) shot on location in China to showcase the range and its AI capabilities. 

 

Product Key Visuals brought each appliance to life within lifestyle contexts—couples and families interacting with everything from washers to ovens to air conditioning units. Each visual told a micro-story: "Smart cycles, better control" or "Smart cooling, effortless savings.” 

Sales Enablement Materials included a detailed product brochure layering technical specifications with emotional benefits, digital banners for media buys, and an immersive product display zone concept designed for retail booths, event spaces and distributor showrooms

Message from the

Dear Shareholders, I am pleased to address you at the close of what has been a remarkable and transformative year for Voltas. The year was marked by heightened global volatility and uncertainty, but also by renewed opportunities for growth and leadership. In the face of shifting dynamics, the Company remained resilient, agile, and future-focussed, delivering record-breaking results while deepening its connection with customers and reinforcing its leadership in key segments.

The year 2024-25 unfolded against a backdrop of rising global uncertainty. What began as a measured recovery soon gave way to a far more intricate economic and geopolitical environment. Mounting inflationary pressures, fuelled by lingering supply disruptions and volatile energy prices, led to a tightening of monetary policies across major economies. Investor confidence declined, capital flows became more risk-averse, and forecasts for global growth were revised downward to a sobering 2.8% for 2025 and 3.0% for 2026—well below historical norms. Compounding these challenges, escalating trade tensions between the United States and its key counterparts further fragmented global supply chains, disrupted policy coordination, and added to overall market volatility. For Voltas, with a footprint spanning diverse markets, this entailed navigating an increasingly dynamic and often challenging external environment with agility, strategic prudence, and foresight.

Yet, amid the global fog, India stands tall. Driven by the twin engines of domestic consumption and demographic strength, the Indian economy continued to defy gravity. Lower crude oil prices, proactive fiscal and monetary policies, and growing investor confidence in India’s long-term potential functioned as powerful stabilisers. This presented an opportunity to deepen our roots in the domestic market, strengthen our consumer connection, and refine our operational execution. While we continued to recalibrate our international portfolio to mitigate risk, we doubled down on our strengths at home, and the results speak for themselves.

Our Performance: A Record-breaking Year

2024-25 marked a defining chapter in the journey of Voltas—not only for the highest-ever consolidated revenues and substantial profitability growth, but more importantly, for the underlying strength of volume-led expansion. We delivered our highest-ever consolidated total income of ₹ 15,737 crores in 2024-25 as compared to ₹ 12,734 crores in 2023-24, a growth of 24%. Our Profit before Tax grew to ₹ 1,191 crores in 2024-25 as compared to ₹ 486 crores in 2023-24, recording a growth of 145%. Coming to our Profit after Tax for the year 2024-25, we posted ₹ 834 crores, as against ₹ 248 crores in 2023-24, registering a substantial growth of 236%. These numbers are not just metrics. They are symbols of a company that continues to strengthen its momentum and sharpen its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving market. Our performance was driven by strong consumer demand for Air Conditioners with advanced features and energy-efficient technologies. The summer surge, coupled with the efforts of our In-shop Demonstrators (ISDs), further contributed to robust performance across all product categories, especially in the Room Air Conditioner (RAC) category. In addition, our omni-channel strategies like expansion of EBOs, strengthening online presence, promotions and campaigns helped us achieve this growth.

The overall volume growth for the UCP Segment for the year was 36%. Voltas became the first brand in India to exceed the milestone of over 2.5 million units of AC sold in a single fiscal year. This extraordinary milestone was underpinned by multiple strategic initiatives.

Our Electro-Mechanical Projects (MEP) business successfully executed projects, internationally and domestically, reinforcing our leadership in commercial and industrial cooling. We also benefitted from a continued push towards cost optimisation, and internal process improvements. These Company-wide initiatives strengthened our margins and supported sustainable growth across business segments.

This performance was further enabled by a strategic ramp up of our manufacturing capacity to cater to the surge in demand. To support future growth and enhance our competitive positioning, we also initiated steps to further scale up our production capacity at our Chennai facility. We deepened our penetration across Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns through retail expansion and stronger last-mile connectivity. Our portfolio was expanded to include Wi-Fi-enabled, inverter based, and eco-friendly Air Conditioners.

Data-led consumer insights enabled more accurate targeting and demand forecasting. Moreover, an agile supply chain guaranteed product availability even during peak summer season. Despite intensifying competition and pricing pressures, we sustained our market leadership, reaffirming Voltas as India’s most trusted cooling brand. Our Air Cooler product category also rebounded robustly in 2024-25, propelled by targeted channel strategies, new product launches, and increasing institutional demand.

ERM Framework 
Voltas has implemented a comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, aligning with 
global best practices such as ISO 31000 and the Committee of Sponsoring Organisations of the Treadway 
Commission (COSO). This framework reflects the Company’s commitment to identifying, assessing, and 
managing both current and potential risks, while also seizing opportunities that can enhance business 
value and support achieving strategic goals. By fostering a robust risk governance structure, Voltas 
aims to enable informed decision-making across all levels of the organisation. The framework focusses 
on creating a resilient approach to managing enterprise, business unit, and functional risks, ensuring 
proactive mitigation strategies. Clear roles and responsibilities have been defined for key stakeholders, with 
standardised reporting tools in place to facilitate the continuous monitoring and assessment of risk profiles 
throughout the organisation. 

The Company undertakes thorough risk identification processes, which are aligned with its strategic goals and the dynamic nature of the business environment. This approach ensures timely identification of both existing and emerging risks that could impact the organisation.

Utilising standardised risk assessment criteria, the Company evaluates potential risks based on their impact, likelihood, and the speed at which they could affect the business. Risks are classified into categories—Critical, High, Medium, and Low—based on the overall assessment score to ensure a focussed approach to risk management.

Voltas recorded robust growth during the year, delivering strong performance across key business segments. This success was driven by multiple factors. This included exceptional performance in the Unitary Cooling Products segment, which benefited from rising temperatures and evolving consumer lifestyles. The increasing preference for Air-Conditioning solutions and cooling appliances as essentials, rather than luxuries has further driven demand.
